text: Cycles can be ridden on the ground or on a bike (cycling bike) or by pedal-powered means such as bicycles or tricycles (two-wheeled vehicles). Brakes are placed at the rear of the front wheel, and tires are placed in the front wheel. Tires are often made of rubber and have a small amount of air in them to inflate when the rider goes down on the ground. Brakes are usually made of iron, and have a small area on the rim called the brake pad. The brake pad fits into the hub, which is the wheel at the back of the bike. When the rider pedals, the brake pad moves up and down, and this causes the brake to make contact with the tire. The brake system is usually controlled by a controller on the handlebar, which is attached to the rear of the bike. The controller is usually a combination of two pedals, one on each side of the bike.
